objective: Standard statement: for each exact family found by ticket A prove its solution structure on every torus, its exactness (which scales, the number of extensions) and its rigidity on the infinite lattice (two distinct solutions differ in infinitely many sites), and conclude under the source-aware reading that no knot is native at any of its solutions. Families: parity on up triangles (exact at scale 2 by (1+S)^2 = 1 + S^2 over the two-element field, with N(2m) = N(m)^2; not exact at scale 3); parity and the three-excluded laws on all triangles (frozen three-colouring patterns, exact at scale 2, not at scale 3); twisted not-all-equal on all triangles (configurations constant along lines of one direction, exact at every scale). Nearest known result: Newman and Moore (1999), fractal symmetries of the plaquette model; Baxter and Wu (1973) ground states; linear cellular automata rescaling (Willson; Allouche et al.). Classification: known-with-delta (the families are classical or elementary; the delta is the census context and the rigidity reading).
status: Proved by SHARED-SUBDIVISION-20261029-001B-P001 (V1, prose plus certified computation): parity on up triangles (Newman-Moore) is exact at scale 2 with N(2m) = N(m)^2 ((1 + S)^2 = 1 + S^2 over the two-element field), not at scale 3, and rigid on the plane; parity on all triangles (Baxter-Wu) has colour-class solutions, is exact at scale 2 (2 permutes the classes), not at 3, and rigid; twisted not-all-equal collapses to the 2^L line-constant configurations (walls persist), exact at every scale, no triangle carries a knot, not rigid (half-lines); the twelve three-excluded rules equal Baxter-Wu on tori of side 2 to 11 (not explained locally); exactness on genuine two-dimensional space keeps a knot only through parity.
title: The exact two-dimensional laws: Newman-Moore, Baxter-Wu ground states and line collapse, and what they keep of emergence
